name: static-joiner
context: A stream must be enriched with reference data that changes rarely — currency and geo tables, product catalogues, feature flags, model metadata, tenant configuration — so issuing a network query or a shard lookup per record is both slow and wasteful. The static joiner materialises the small side of the join locally (broadcast to every worker, or replicated into a compacted changelog and read as a table) and joins in-process, trading memory and replication cost for the removal of a per-record remote call.
benefits: Eliminates a per-record network round trip — the join becomes an in-memory probe against a local store
Removes load from the authoritative reference store, which is often the very system the join exists to protect
Broadcasting the reference side removes the co-partitioning requirement entirely, so the stream need not be re-keyed to match it
Reference data can be refreshed without restarting the stream: the local copy is updated from a changelog
Chainable — several small reference tables can be joined in sequence without extra shuffles, unlike a repartitioned table join
tradeoffs: Every worker holds a full copy, so local memory and broker read bandwidth scale with workers times reference size
The join is only as fresh as the last reference update — a stale local copy silently produces wrong enrichment
A reference table that outgrows memory turns a static join into an unbounded problem that must be redesigned
Broadcasting a partitioned topic multiplies broker read load by the consumer count, which can become its own bottleneck
Foreign-key-style lookups by a value other than the record key are supported by global tables but not by co-partitioned local tables
use_cases: Enriching clickstream events with campaign and referrer metadata held in a slowly changing reference topic
Annotating transactions with currency and exchange-rate reference data for reporting
Joining IoT readings with a device registry that is provisioned rarely but queried constantly
Applying tenant configuration and feature flags to a high-volume stream without calling the config service per record
Star joins in which a fact stream meets several small dimension topics in sequence
avoid_when: The reference side is large, unbounded or changes at a rate comparable to the stream
A per-record external lookup is already cheap and the reference store is designed for point reads
Strong consistency with the authoritative reference store is required at the moment of the join
The reference data is itself highly partitioned and co-partitioned access is acceptable
component_types: Reference source: compacted topic, snapshot file, or change-data-capture stream from the authoritative store
Global/local reference table: fully replicated on every worker, or a partitioned table read as a local store
Broadcast join operator: per-key lookup into the local copy with no co-partitioning requirement
External lookup operator: async call to the authoritative store, used when the reference cannot be replicated
Refresh mechanism: changelog consumption or periodic reload that updates the local copy in place
Size guard: threshold that converts the join from broadcast to lookup when the reference exceeds the budget
technology_stack: Apache Spark (broadcast hash join, BROADCAST hint)
anti_patterns: Broadcasting a reference topic whose size has quietly outgrown the memory budget
Re-keying the stream to co-partition with a reference topic when a global broadcast join would need no repartition
Treating the local copy as authoritative and never reconciling it against the source of truth
Choosing a join strategy at plan time from estimated sizes, when runtime statistics would have chosen better
Joining against a reference topic that is not compacted, so the local copy accumulates every historical revision
design_principles: Replicate the small side, never the large one
Local-first joins: reference data belongs next to the processor, not behind a socket
No co-partitioning requirement for globally replicated reference data
Freshness is an explicit property of the join, measured and bounded
A size budget decides the strategy — broadcast below it, lookup above it
best_practices: Compact the reference topic so each key retains only its latest value
Track reference-table size in bytes, not row count, when sizing the broadcast budget
Set an explicit size threshold that flips the join strategy before the local copy becomes fatal
Keep the join key identical to the reference key; a foreign-key lookup needs a global table, not a partitioned one
Monitor the staleness of the local copy as a first-class pipeline SLI
